statement.p: Find an equation of the plane through the three points given:

static.solution:
\mathbf{n}\cdot \left\lt x,y,z\right>=d
To find the normal vector to the plane, \mathbf{n}, we first compute the vectors \vec{PQ} and \vec{PR} that lie in the plane, and then find the cross product of these vectors. This gives:
\vec{PQ}= \left\lt 4,4,-1\right> - \left\lt 0,0,1\right> = \left\lt 4,4,-2\right>
\vec{PR}= \left\lt -2,1,-2\right> - \left\lt 0,0,1\right> = \left\lt -2,1,-3\right>
\mathbf{n} = \vec{PQ}\times \vec{PR} = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \boldsymbol{i} \amp \boldsymbol{j} \amp \boldsymbol{k} \\ 4 \amp 4 \amp -2 \\ -2 \amp 1 \amp -3 \end{array} \right|
\qquad = \left| \begin{array}{cc} 4 \amp -2 \\ 1 \amp -3 \end{array} \right| \boldsymbol{i} -\left| \begin{array}{cc} 4 \amp -2 \\ -2 \amp -3 \end{array} \right| \boldsymbol{j} +\left| \begin{array}{cc} 4 \amp 4 \\ -2 \amp 1 \end{array} \right| \boldsymbol{k}
\qquad =-10 \boldsymbol{i} + 16 \boldsymbol{j} + 12 \boldsymbol{k}
We now choose any of the three points in the plane, say P=\left(0,0,1\right), and compute d.
d=\mathbf{n} \cdot\vec{OP}=\left\lt -10,16,12\right> \cdot \left\lt 0,0,1\right> = 12
Finally we obtain the following equation of the plane:
-10 x + 16 y + 12 z = 12.
